channel.title: Blindspot
channel.description: Independent, rigorous analysis of geopolitics, global economy, security, technology, and power. What mainstream coverage leaves out.

item.title: Far-right attack in Krakow exposes growing domestic security vulnerabilities in Central Europe
item.description: A lethal shooting in Poland's historic center has left nine people dead, including victims found at the suspect's home. The incident reveals how domestic extremism is evading Central European intelligence frameworks.

item.title: Asymmetric Aerial Attacks Escalating in Rural Colombia Target Military Base Infrastructure
item.description: A lethal drone attack in Bolívar left three dead and up to sixteen soldiers wounded. The strike highlights how modified commercial drones are fundamentally altering rural security dynamics.

item.title: Israel President Taps Gadi Eisenkot to Form Government as Netanyahu Faces Removal
item.description: President Isaac Herzog has granted former military chief Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form Israel's next government. The decision threatens Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure but exposes deep ideological fractures within the opposition alliance.

item.title: SoftBank and ABB explore China carve-out to salvage robotics deal
item.description: SoftBank and ABB are weighing a strategic carve-out of their Chinese operations to rescue a $5.4 billion robotics transaction from regulatory impasse. The move underscores the growing impossibility of maintaining integrated global tech portfolios amidst hardening geopolitical lines.

item.title: Automated offensive tools trigger systemic crisis across global cybersecurity infrastructure
item.description: Artificial intelligence is enabling state actors and hostile groups to discover and exploit software vulnerabilities simultaneously. Security experts warn of a transitional dark age as defensive protocols fail to keep pace.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV Begins South American Tour in Secular Uruguay Following Surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay less than a month after undergoing lung surgery. Beyond pastoral gestures, the trip tests Vatican soft power in South America's most secular state.

item.title: Paraguay Prosecutors Indict Former President Santiago Peña Following Ueno Bank Collapse
item.description: Paraguayan authorities have ordered the detention and asset freeze of former President Santiago Peña over financial crimes. The move exposes deep vulnerabilities in the country's banking oversight and governance structure.

item.title: Mass Shooting in Krakow Historic Center Leaves Six Dead and 15 Injured
item.description: A deadly shooting in Poland's second-largest city has claimed six lives and wounded 15 others. Beyond the immediate emergency response lies a complex debate over internal policing priorities in Central Europe.

item.title: Syria denies troop deployments to Yemen as military channels with Saudi Arabia open
item.description: Damascus has rejected reports of active military support for Saudi anti-Houthi efforts. Yet the diplomatic signaling points toward an expanding security dialogue between two former regional adversaries.

item.title: The Structural Realities Behind the 2026 U.S. Senate Midterm Map
item.description: As the 2026 U.S. Senate elections approach, thirty-five seats are up for grabs across an unforgiving electoral map. Controlling the chamber requires navigating tight margins, special elections, and structural legislative hurdles.

item.title: US Export Controls Fail as Nvidia AI Chips Reach Empty Chinese Shell Firms
item.description: Federal regulators have cleared advanced Nvidia processors for distribution to Chinese entities with empty offices and blacklisted backers. The lapse highlights the structural conflicts of a revenue-sharing export model.

item.title: Inside the House GOP revolt as Stephen Miller takes the West Wing helm
item.description: President Donald Trump's decision to appoint Stephen Miller as chief of staff has triggered open rebellion among congressional Republicans. The move deepens internal party fractures following historic midterm losses.

item.title: How the wider Iran war shattered Yemen's fragile truce and reignited a dormant conflict
item.description: Fresh airstrikes reported near Sanaa have left dozens dead, exposing how regional escalation with Iran immediately broke Yemen's fragile ceasefire. The United Nations reports that more than 1,600 people have been killed since major hostilities resumed.

item.title: An armed attack in Krakow exposes the security vulnerabilities of open European public squares
item.description: Five people are dead and at least 10 injured following a shooting near the main market square in Krakow. The incident highlights the persistent difficulty of securing dense urban environments against sudden localized violence.

item.title: Guatemalan Lawmaker Murder Highlights Rising Political Risk Ahead of National Elections
item.description: An armed ambush in eastern Guatemala leaves a member of congress and three officers dead. The attack underscores the lethal overlap between organized crime corridors and national political party realignment.
